# Pax Silica vs WAICO: Will Central Asia Have to Pick a Side?

The Diplomat (Crossroads Asia / Economy / Central Asia), by Catherine Putz (managing editor), September 8, 2026. Full article retrieved (paywalled after 2 free articles, but full text present on page).

## Key findings
- **Kazakhstan** is the only country to have joined both Pax Silica and WAICO. Astana joined Pax Silica officially on **June 27, 2026** (Deputy PM and Minister of AI and Digital Development Zhaslan Madiyev signed the declaration and joint statement on the AI Opportunity Partnership at the second Pax Silica Summit in Washington, D.C.). Less than three weeks later, Madiyev attended WAIC 2026 in Shanghai and became a **founding member of WAICO alongside 28 other countries**.
- **Counts**: Pax Silica counts **24 countries** as signatories (Taiwan listed as a "non-signatory participant"); Beijing counts **37 countries** as members of WAICO (Bangladesh as "observer").
- **Pax Silica** (launched Dec 2025) is branded by the US State Department as its "flagship effort on AI and supply chain security, advancing new economic security consensus among allies and trusted partners." Declaration highlights supply-chain resilience (energy → critical mineral → manufacturing → technology → infrastructure). References to "reducing excessive dependencies" and "forging new connections with reliable partners" are dog whistles at Beijing.
- **WAICO** (proposed July 2025, created July 2026) frames itself as an international organization focused on AI governance. UN Secretary-General António Guterres attended the signing as a guest (impression of UN endorsement).
- **The pick-a-side pressure**: mid-August, Reuters reported an undated draft State Department letter to the 35 signatories of the AI Opportunity Statement: "To be part of everything is to be part of nothing. Signature of the Pax Silica Declaration is not merely a membership subscription, but a commitment." It urged countries to "choose deliberately" on AI and stated Pax Silica membership "cannot be held alongside membership in duplicative initiatives whose expectations conflict with our own." The letter did not directly mention China; as of writing it had not been sent.
- In early August, US Assistant Secretary of State for South and Central Asian Affairs **Paul Kapur** visited several countries incl. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan; in Kazakhstan he met Madiyev to "discuss digital development."
- **Uzbekistan** (like Kazakhstan, joined WAICO in July, as did Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan): in late August, Uzbek ambassador to the US **Furqat Sidikov** said Tashkent had requested to join Pax Silica (diplomatic note sent): "Now, the U.S. should confirm. We are ready to sign." Sidikov called red lines around participation "counterproductive."
- Context: Pax Silica's core areas (critical mineral dependencies) are addressed by the budding US–Central Asia partnership, but per Lemon & Jardine (The Diplomat, April 2026), "the United States is losing the race for Central Asia's critical minerals" — Russia and China remain dominant in the region's critical-minerals mining. Forcing the region to choose may not yield the result Washington wants.

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — The Diplomat is a recognized Asia-Pacific policy outlet; detailed reporting with named officials and primary documents (Reuters draft-letter report, State Dept, qazinform, Astana Times).
